title: Gatebraid guard verdict document (gatebraid/guard-verdict@1)
description: The document `gatebraid-guard` emits at every pre-flight: the normalised facts it evaluated, one result per check in a fixed order, the verdict and the exit status. Introduced at M3 node P as that node's first deliverable (M3-PLAN.md section 2 P; ADR-0036), admitted under ADR-0030 by the milestone authority that introduces it plus the operator's batch approval; it amends ADR-0010 not at all. THE DESIGN RULE: the guard prints what it evaluated, so a verdict can be disputed from the document without re-running the guard, and the schema's conditionals bind the facts to the results, so a document that reports a violating fact beside a passing result is invalid. That is how corpus v2 asserts the twelve checks before the guard exists (ADR-0031's route, as gatebraid/snapshot@1 took it for O0): each negative case is a verdict document a correct guard can never emit. Facts are counts, booleans and closed enumerations; the values the guard forbids -- an identifier outside the set, a truncated SHA, a foreign ref name -- never enter this document (ADR-0028 section 3). `format` is deliberately absent and every timestamp is a lexical `pattern`, for the reason the other frozen interfaces record. The classification of which corpus items assert what against this schema lives in fixtures/CORPUS-v2-PLAN.md, its single home.

source_sha256.description: sha256 of the guard's own source, so a verdict names the evaluator that produced it.

store_is_dedicated.description: GH_CONFIG_DIR in the guard's own environment names the dedicated store (ADR-0024 section 1).

active_is_executor.description: The dedicated store's active login is the executor's machine account (ADR-0022 sections 1 and 4).

account_count.description: How many accounts the dedicated store lists. The roster rule (ADR-0036 decision 3, from friction #92): exactly one, the executor's. A store that lists two is a partition delivered as a pointer.

git_identity_is_executor.description: The clone's repo-local git user.name and user.email are the executor's (ADR-0022 section 1 surface (b)).

identity.description: Check 1. Names are never quoted here: the document says whether the login IS the executor's, not what it is.

identifiers_outside_set.description: Count of owner/name identifiers, across the remote, the snapshot's item and edge references and the state packet, that are not one of the two permitted repositories. A count and positions, never the names (ADR-0028 section 3).

baseline_recorded.description: The Slice's Gate 0 ref listing exists to compare against.

foreign_refs_present.description: Refs outside refs/heads/, refs/remotes/ and refs/tags/ in the working clone now.

foreign_refs_introduced.description: Of those, the ones absent from the Gate 0 baseline listing. ADR-0036 decision 4: introduced is a deny; pre-existing is the doctor's finding.

fields_not_full.description: SHA-bearing fields whose value is not the full object name: 40 hex for a git object, 64 hex for a sha256. The Project's free-text Base SHA and an approval's citation are examined; the schema-checked record fields are the record's own business.

diff_outside.description: Paths in git diff --name-only <base_sha>..<head> outside the frozen write_domains.

untracked_outside.description: Paths in git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all outside the frozen write_domains (gate-2-contract R1; friction #107).

lease_holders_in_repository.description: Open items in the same working repository whose Writer Lease is non-empty, this Slice included (ADR-0003: at most one).

lease.description: Check 6 (ADR-0003; gate-2-contract entry; ADR-0025 section 3; friction #106).

plan_hash_reproduces.description: The recorded plan_hash recomputes from gate1.md's frozen section by the recorded command; null before Gate 1 froze anything.

issue_write_domains_match.description: The Slice issue's gatebraid-metadata write_domains equals the frozen allowlist (gate-1-contract exit; friction #65).

required.description: This gate's entry requires a door (Gate 2, Gate 3).

author_is_operator.description: The observed author login is the operator's personal account (gate-2-contract entry (c); ADR-0020 section 4). Phrased as ADR-0020 phrases it: evidence the executor did not write it, never evidence of human intent (ADR-0015 section 1).

names_both_hashes.description: Gate 2: the comment names plan_hash and allowlist_hash; Gate 3: it states the publication terms.

blocked_reason_needs_input.description: For Workflow = Blocked only: the latest comment's typed reason is needs_input. Null otherwise.

labels.description: Check 9 (spec section 1's coupling table, as written; ADR-0025 decision 5; ADR-0036 decision 5).

degraded_sources.description: Sources whose status is not ok or whose read is incomplete (gatebraid/snapshot@1 $defs/degradedSource).

verdict_consumed.description: The frontier verdict this pre-flight would act on; null when none is consumed.

tree_unchanged.description: git rev-parse <attempt>^{tree} equals the tree at the previous failed state (gate-2-contract, ADR-0027 section 1).

repairs.description: Check 11: an unchanged tree is not a repair; it may only be recorded consumed and still_red.

baseline_tracked.description: A hook baseline document is tracked in the control repository (R-min authors it). While none is, the check denies (ADR-0036 decision 6).

matches_baseline.description: The host's hook surface equals the tracked baseline; null while no baseline is tracked.

facts.description: Normalised inputs, one group per check, in the plan's order. Every group is required: a guard that did not read a group cannot claim a verdict (it says not_evaluated).

rule.description: The governing sentence by file and line (CORPUS-v2-PLAN.md section 2 names each).

trace.description: What was evaluated, normalised: enough to dispute the verdict without re-running the guard, and never a forbidden value.

checks.description: Exactly twelve entries, one per check id (coverage is asserted by the allOf entries below), in the plan's order.

exit_code.description: 0 allow, 1 deny, 2 the guard could not evaluate. A closed set; the exit status decides (spec section 4).

allOf.$comment: Coverage: every verdict carries a `identity` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-identity).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `closed_set` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-closed_set).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `ref_namespaces` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-ref_namespaces).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `full_sha` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-full_sha).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `allowlist` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-allowlist).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `writer_lease` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-writer_lease).

Coverage: every verdict carries a `plan_allowlist_hash` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-plan_allowlist_hash).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `approval_author` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-approval_author).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `label_coupling` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-label_coupling).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `snapshot_flags` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-snapshot_flags).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `repair_novelty` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-repair_novelty).
Coverage: every verdict carries a `hooks_enabled` entry. Twelve of these, one per check id, so that a guard that silently skipped a check cannot emit a valid document (GV1-15-hooks_enabled).
Strictest wins (ADR-0036 decision 2): any `deny` makes the verdict `deny` (GV1-14).
`allow` is the verdict only when every check passed (GV1-14's second locus).
`not_evaluated` is the verdict only when some check could not be evaluated and none denied; a deny outranks it (GV1-19, GV1-19b).
Closed exit set (ADR-0036 decision 2; spec section 4 'the exit status decides'): verdict `allow` is exit 0 (GV1-16-allow).
Closed exit set (ADR-0036 decision 2; spec section 4 'the exit status decides'): verdict `deny` is exit 1 (GV1-16-deny).
Closed exit set (ADR-0036 decision 2; spec section 4 'the exit status decides'): verdict `not_evaluated` is exit 2 (GV1-16-not_evaluated).
A deny is disputable from its trace: a denying check carries at least one trace line and a non-empty detail (GV1-17).
Check 1, identity: GH_CONFIG_DIR in the guard's own environment must name the dedicated store (ADR-0024 section 1) (GV1-01)
Check 1, identity: the dedicated store's active login must be the executor's; drift is a stop (ADR-0022 section 4) (GV1-01b)
Check 1, identity: surface (b), the clone's git author and committer identity, must be the executor's (ADR-0022 section 1) (GV1-01c)
Check 1, identity: the roster rule (ADR-0036 decision 3, from friction #92): the store lists exactly one account; a partition delivered as a pointer is a deny (GV1-02)
Check 2, closed_set: one identifier outside the permitted set is a deny; the count is what the document carries, the identifier never is (GV1-03)
Check 3, ref_namespaces: a foreign ref introduced since the Gate 0 baseline is a deny; one present at the baseline is the doctor's finding (ADR-0036 decision 4) (GV1-04)
Check 4, full_sha: a SHA-bearing field that is not the full object name is a deny (ADR-0029 P1-1; ADR-0028 section 2) (GV1-05)
Check 5, allowlist: a changed path outside the frozen write_domains is a deny (gate-2-contract R1) (GV1-06)
Check 5, allowlist: an untracked path outside the frozen write_domains is a deny -- a write created and removed inside the gate is invisible to the diff (friction #107) (GV1-06b)
Check 6, writer_lease: inside the lease-holding states (Gate 2 entry through Gate 3 exit) with no lease is a deny (ADR-0003; friction #106) (GV1-07)
Check 6, writer_lease: more than one lease holder in a repository is a deny (ADR-0003: a second writer is a stop-the-line event) (GV1-07b)
Check 6, writer_lease: a lease surviving Aborted is a deny (ADR-0025 section 3 clears it; a terminated Slice must not obstruct a successor) (GV1-07c)
Check 7, plan_allowlist_hash: a plan_hash that does not recompute by its recorded command is a deny (gate-1-contract row 6: a hash nobody can recompute is decoration) (GV1-08)
Check 7, plan_allowlist_hash: an allowlist_hash that does not recompute is a deny (gate-1-contract) (GV1-08b)
Check 7, plan_allowlist_hash: an issue body whose write_domains differs from the frozen allowlist is a deny (gate-1-contract exit; friction #65) (GV1-08c)
Check 8, approval_author: where a door is required and no approval is found, the gate does not enter (gate-3-contract 'outside this table') (GV1-09)

Check 8, approval_author: an approval authored by any account other than the operator's is invalid as if absent (gate-2-contract entry (c); ADR-0020 section 4); the executor as author is the next row's own case (GV1-09b)

Check 8, approval_author: an approval authored by the executing session is a deny -- ADR-0020 section 4's evidence runs the other way: the author being the operator is evidence the executor did not write it, never evidence of human intent (ADR-0015 section 1) (GV1-09c)

Check 8, approval_author: an approval that does not name both hashes (Gate 2) or the publication terms (Gate 3) is not the approval of this authorisation (gate-2-contract entry (b); ADR-0018 section 3) (GV1-09d)
Check 9, label_coupling: needs-human off in state 4, 9 or 11 is a deny (spec section 1's table as written; ADR-0036 decision 5) (GV1-10)

Check 9, label_coupling: needs-human on outside states 4, 9, 11 and Blocked is a deny; friction #230's choreography dispute is a prose amendment to ADR-0025, not the guard's to adjudicate (ADR-0036 decision 5) (GV1-10b)
Check 9, label_coupling: Blocked carries the label only with a needs_input-typed reason; the label on with another reason is a deny (spec section 1) (GV1-10c)
Check 9, label_coupling: Blocked with a needs_input-typed reason and no label is a deny (spec section 1; gate-0-contract) (GV1-10d)
Check 10, snapshot_flags: no snapshot is a deny: startability is read from a snapshot or not claimed (M3-PLAN P0-4; ADR-0025 section 8) (GV1-11)
Check 10, snapshot_flags: a degraded source beside any verdict other than undecidable is a deny (M3-PLAN P0-3/P0-4; gatebraid/snapshot@1's fail-closed conditional) (GV1-11b)
Check 11, repair_novelty: an attempt whose tree is unchanged and whose result is not still_red is a deny: an unchanged tree is not a repair (gate-2-contract; ADR-0027 section 1) (GV1-12)
Check 12, hooks_enabled: while no hook baseline is tracked the check denies; R-min lands the baseline (ADR-0036 decision 6) (GV1-13)
Check 12, hooks_enabled: a host hook surface that does not match the tracked baseline is a deny (ADR-0036 decision 6) (GV1-13b)
